terms.comment: The modern word, made on ēlectrum, amber (Greek ἤλεκτρον), which classically is amber or the alloy of gold and silver (Lewis & Short). Traupman’s e-mail is litterae ēlectronicae or epistula ēlectronica (p. 260–261), an e-mail address īnscrīptiō ēlectronica (p. 261). Morgan–Owens writes electrônicus with a long o; we follow Traupman, whose short o the lexicon already uses.

phrases.english: I’ll send you an e-mail tomorrow.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 260–261 (ēlectronicus, litterae ēlectronicae, īnscrīptiō ēlectronica), 309. Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. electronic.
The example sentence marked “composed” is ours.
